title: Stream norm-six features with 320 live integer slots (no κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Generate all 19,600 source/target feature pairs for the actual norm-six kernel in one pass, without a per-feature transform table or a target accumulator array. The new indexed-integer contract needs **320 live integer slots**, including both borrowed 48-coordinate inputs, plus the fixed **2,304-slot Gram matrix**. Each output record must be consumed and released before the next is requested; retained outputs are additional caller storage.

The construction uses a dyadic-unit two-coordinate pivot and locally generated coefficients. The accompanying proof bounds every preprocessing intermediate by 19 signed bits and the complete stream by 159,389 multiplications, 61,150 additions/subtractions, 96 exact divisions by three, two pivot divisions by two and at most 144 public diagonal halvings. It also charges indexed accesses. These are upper bounds in the stated abstract machine model, not CPython heap measurements or a physical routing invoice.

Concurrent JoyboyBrian **#5132** already resolves the original explicit-constructibility question. I credit that result and narrowed the public claim before publication. Its stated evaluator allocates 19,712 target slots, 64 source slots and 245,884 immutable descriptor slots including the Gram. This contribution supplies a different memory/consumer-lifetime contract with no cubic-size descriptor or accumulator; it compares two explicit allocations, not a lower bound on every implementation of #5132. The feature bases differ and cannot be substituted without their matching source features.

**Status:** explicit construction and written algebraic/storage proof, with independent exact corroboration. No improved term count, coefficient optimality, superior total arithmetic cost, full-shell rank, native physical decoder, selected frontier change or new κ. Physical source acquisition, variable-data side programs, frames, owners, dirty restoration, precision, routing and outer admission remain unpriced.

## Task and overlap

- Scope **changed** from the original constructibility handoff in #5084 to the descriptor-free stream; canonical claim and history: [Discussion #5127](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5127), [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5127#discussioncomment-19143848). Entry point was handoffs #1166; current priority revision is 7 and card is `complex-rank-shape-decoder`. The scoped memory interface does not claim the card's whole-supplier/five-percent gate.
- Fresh-clone scientific base: `20a1e31bc6009b9b3f4d084bbaadc6350e34fcba`. Publication rebased onto `a5df48c55ea806d7952b65acc9c76d878ff09b13`; relevant guidance, selected record and pinned scientific sources were unchanged. Proposed head: `c7cffff0dd40b7aa787739cf48b6dc7d776ca2d7`.
- Exact comparison head for #5132: `08572fdb060e73ecc4cb09a024611039881185f4` (merged). Its proof is credited comparison context; its code is not imported. All source pins and their roles are in `SOURCES.json`; only the pinned Gram JSON is a live external input.
- Final live refresh: all **305 open PRs** (10:53:32 UTC), **4,294 Discussion records** (10:54:33 UTC), and **6,920 indexed local notes**, with complete pagination/inventory and no refresh warnings. No competing claim for this stream contract was found; #5132 was separately rechecked as merged at the credited head. All ten Discussion threads authored today by krzysztofwojt were checked, including the new one-slot doubled-centre Gram claim #5142. Reflection-rounding, Schur, A5, doubled-centre and earlier submitted/claimed topics are excluded. Snapshot searches do not establish absence of unpublished work or arbitrary-diff overlap.

**Merge danger: low in both directions.** This adds only ten files under `research/norm6-streaming-features/`, with no shared-code, dependency, frozen-source or selected-record edits. Replays are explicitly registered; no heavy default suite is introduced.

## Validation

Python 3.12.12, macOS arm64, standard library only. At the proposed head:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/norm6-streaming-features
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/norm6-streaming-features --check-source-history
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py export --package research/norm6-streaming-features --ref HEAD --output /tmp/norm6-streaming-features.tar
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py check /tmp/norm6-streaming-features.tar
```

- Registered normal and optimized (`-O`) isolated, warning-as-error replays pass: `PASS_NORM6_STREAMING_FEATURES` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.
- Independent polynomial-convolution oracle: 48 relation rows / 43,056 coefficient comparisons; all 2,304 entries of the pivot-inverse certificate; 3,275 small-dimensional and five full-dimensional target polynomial identities.
- All 3,449,600 emitted coordinates across 176 complete streams agree exactly with the independently checked reference. Tests cover ordering, borrowed inputs, four owned vectors, completion/early close, a nonzero off-shell defect and 13 rejecting controls. The 44 actual-shell vectors are diagnostic, not a full-shell enumeration. Universal coverage comes from the proof.
- Exact inverse multiplication establishes the coordinate bound 32 under the cited positive-definiteness premise. Static inspection proves storage; finite Python frame inventories only corroborate it.
- Four disposable code mutations (relation coefficient, pivot-inverse sign, triple multiplicity, streamed coefficient) reject on mathematical mismatches with the receipt hash gate bypassed. A Boolean-for-zero receipt corruption also rejects under `-O`.
- Publication bytes and declared source ancestry pass (11 files, including the Gram input). Official export/integrity check passes. Both verifier modes pass again from a fresh read-only export with `PATH=/nonexistent`, no Git or predecessor executable; all 12 file hashes including the export receipt remain unchanged. Export SHA256: `b55caeedd419448353c769689e306efc33edfbff9a1d050bde35c62d4474e9f1`.
- `git diff --check` passes. Hosted [CI run 39942609405](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39942609405) passes at exact head `c7cffff0dd40b7aa787739cf48b6dc7d776ca2d7`: both `plan` (including shared helper tests) and the registered package replay are successful. No human review, formal proof-kernel acceptance or physical integration is claimed. Shared/heavy suites were not run locally.

## Credit

Nick Petalas (#5084, `9d7f7805d147028fe5f0174e267ee05b73703f0b`) supplied the dyadic existence result and handoff. JoyboyBrian (#5132, exact head above) independently supplied explicit constructibility and resource bounds. DreamingOfClouds (#2244, `8ef6fa81403973d3cacaf865bdabe9797a6c34a0`) and David Ganz / Dugongue (#4494, `ad31d9fdf000d4ca98dd911afe489a45d2ea4f74`) retain credit for the rational shell-rank perspective and dyadic factorization lineage. Nebe/Sloane and the inherited lattice/kernel lineage remain credited; classical elimination and Cauchy–Schwarz are not new techniques.

Prepared by Krzysztof Wojt with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Bounded Luna support covered the overlap inventory, independently authored polynomial oracle and arithmetic/storage review; the primary agent reviewed and integrated the work. Apache-2.0; no predecessor source/license was changed.

## Open next questions

Can one actual chronological physical source/target caller consume each feature without retaining a cubic-size array and still have a favorable complete invoice? The smallest useful follow-up is to bind one invocation, check ordering and lifetime, and charge acquisition, preparation, retained outputs, frames, owners, restoration, precision and tape placement. A physical caller is the blocker; the generator alone does not resolve it. Details: `research/norm6-streaming-features/README.md#open-next-questions` and `TASK.json`.
